findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the back door of the facility to be slightly open. A window with no screen was also open. PIC was informed that outer openings of the facility need to be protected to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the air conditioning system above the prep table to be soiled with grease accumulation and dust. The hood above the pizza oven was also heavily soiled with grease and dust. These non-food contact surfaces pose a cross-contamination risk, as the dust can fall directly onto food and food contact surfaces. Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation : Inspector observed floors and walls around dough mixing machines to be soiled with flour dust. Clean floors and walls around dough machine. 

Repeat Violation : Inspector observed the floor of the walk-in freezer to be soiled with food debris. Ensure this space is cleaned frequently.

Inspector observed the prep cooler top to be heavily soiled with food residue. Ensure the prep cooler is cleaned thoroughly (including under and behind lid to prep top).
The bottom of the 2-door cooler in the back room had standing murky water. Ensure this cooler is cleaned to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Observed a mop stored in the bottom of a dump sink in the back maintenance area. PIC was informed that mop heads need to be stored hanging so that they can drip dry. Mops left sitting on a surface can promote bacterial accumulation and cause cross-contamination. Ensure staff are hanging mop heads to drip dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation : Observed bare wood being used to hold paper towel dispenser to wall in cook area. Bare wood is absorbent, and is therefore not considered smooth or easily cleanable. Either seal wood or replace with a different material prior to next routine inspection. 

Repeat Violation : Observed caulking in need of repair around hand sink in cooking area as well as around the triple sink. Caulking ensures that there is no soil accumulation between equipment and walls, and also creates a smooth surface for cleaning. Ensure the caulking is replaced prior to next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at the beginning of the inspection. A manager was called and arrived during the inspection. Ensure there is a CFPM present at all times of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the employee bathroom to have no paper towels. Paper towels are necessary for handwashing using a protective barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure there are paper towels in the restroom at all times. The bathroom was supplied properly during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the triple sink sanitizing station to read 10ppm chlorine. The employee handling dishwashing was made aware of the concentration was too low, and the triple sink was prepared with new sanitizer. The new sanitizer concentration as 100ppm chlorine. 

It was also observed that there were no sanitizer buckets prepared on the prep or cook line during the time of inspection. The PIC was able to educate staff on proper bucket preparation and triple sink setup. The new buckets measured 100ppm chlorine. Ensure a sanitizer buckets with cloths is available at all times of food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed coving throughout the kitchen and dry storage areas to be damaged or missing. Coving is essential for proper cleaning of the floors and walls in a food prep area. The floor wall junctures being properly sealed also inhibits the movement of pests throughout the facility. Ensure the coving in the food preparation and storage areas is repaired before the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the gasket of the white standing freezer to be broken. The gasket is necessary for proper sealing of the freezer. Ensure the seal is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Multiple personal drinks and a granola bar were observed to be stored on the upper-shelf of a cooler with food for consumers. Personal items need to be stored in a designated space away from food for consumers to prevent cross-contamination. This designated area can be a dedicated cooler or the bottom shelf of a cooler to prevent personal food falling onto food for consumers. Ensure a designated area is used for personal items prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC was unable to find any food handler’s certificates on file. The CFPM is from another location, so is unsure of the location of the paper work. Ensure food handler’s certificates are available for view at the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available for use in employee bathroom. Paper towels were provided during inspection. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizing solution in use at facility to contain bleach and dish detergent. Sanitizing solution was remade during inspection and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.comment:
Observed container on shelf under prep table to be soiled with food and liquid debris. Container was placed at 3 compartment sink during inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed facility to not have signed reporting agreements for all food employees. Provide signed employee reporting agreements for all food employees.

2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed in wall air conditioner in kitchen to have openings to the outside. Remove air conditioner or fill openings. 

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizing solution available for use during food preparation. Sanitizing solution was made and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed facility to not have food handler training certifications for all food employees. Provide food handler certification for all food employees.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  
Found the pizza make table out of temperature. The employee/pic is unaware that the table is not maintaining temperature.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 
Ghel’s cheese machine is holding at 124F. The bag of cheese was discarded and the machine removed from service. A new machine was ordered.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.
The pizza make table is not holding items at proper temperature. Items in the top are 48 to 50 degrees Ferinheight. The bottom of the unit is holding food between 52 and 54 degrees Ferinheight. The make table has been emptied and the items were discarded. A list of discarded items accompanies the report.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 
A wet wiping cloth was observed to be sitting on the prep table upon entry. Wiping cloth was moved to the sanitizer bucket.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 
Door seals on the make table and on the 2 door reach in in the prep area are no longer intact and/or adjusted properly. Repair/replace the seals on these unit doors.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 
The wall by the restroom, in the storage area combined with the office, is in disrepair. Inspector was informed that there had been a water leak in the area. Repair wall so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
